chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Aban ibn Uthman from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' al-Razi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

‘I'tikaf (seclusion in a mosque) is not valid except in a mosque of the congregation.’ The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh al-Tusi) said: And it has been narrated that it is not valid except in a mosque in which a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet has led the prayer. (882) 14 Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated this - from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), ‘What do you say about ‘I'tikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques?’ He said, ‘There is no ‘I'tikaf except in a mosque of the congregation in which a just Imam has led the congregational prayer, and there is no harm in performing ‘I'tikaf in the mosque of Kufa, the mosque of Medina, and the mosque of Mecca.’

key_terms.إِمَامٌ عَدْلٌ: A just Imam (a leader of prayer who is just and qualified)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ جَمَاعَةٍ: Mosque of the congregation (a mosque where congregational prayer is regularly held)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of I'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the juristic requirement for 'I'tikaf by linking its validity to the presence of a just Imam leading congregational prayer, a condition that distinguishes major sanctuaries like Kufa and Medina from other mosques. The text highlights the scholarly debate regarding whether 'I'tikaf is restricted exclusively to mosques associated with Prophets or Imams, or if it extends to any mosque where a qualified Imam leads the community, thereby emphasizing the spiritual and communal dimensions of seclusion.
